agencies.name: Ministry of Environment and Forestry (KLHK)
agencies.role: Issued the regulation that defines Indonesia's air pollution standard index (ISPU) and how it must be published.

agencies.name: Ministry of Health
agencies.role: Records respiratory infections during haze. Al Jazeera reported more than 170,000 recorded in 2026.

nationalIndex.name: Indeks Standar Pencemar Udara (ISPU)
nationalIndex.description: Defined by Minister of Environment and Forestry Regulation P.14/MENLHK/SETJEN/KUM.1/7/2020. Covers PM10, PM2.5, CO, NO2, SO2, O3 and hydrocarbons, with five categories from 'baik' (good) to 'berbahaya' (hazardous). The ISPU is calculated hourly.

monitoring.text: The 2020 regulation requires PM2.5 information to be published to the public every hour, and other parameters at least twice a day.

seasonalPattern.text: In 2015 the government reported 2.6 million hectares burned between June and October, about a third of it peatland, according to the World Bank.
A CIFOR satellite assessment estimated 1.64 million hectares burned between January and October 2019, 41 percent of it peatland, as reported by The Jakarta Post.

healthContext.text: The World Bank cites more than 500,000 acute respiratory infection cases and 19 haze-related deaths in 2015.

policy.text: Indonesia's parliament approved ratification of the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution through Law No. 26 of 2014, and the instrument was deposited on 20 January 2015.
Regulation P.14/MENLHK/SETJEN/KUM.1/7/2020 on the ISPU was enacted.

openQuestions: ISPU category ranges are in an annex of the regulation that could not be read in the copy checked.
The number and location of ISPU stations, and any public data access route, are not documented here.
Official 2026 burned-area and hotspot totals have not been sourced from KLHK.
